# Carbon Energy Nexus

> A free daily publication at carbonenergynexus.com on where carbon, energy, water and capital meet: CO2 capture and storage, carbon markets and removals, energy policy, produced water and the water footprint of energy, project finance and research. Each edition sorts news by electrons (power), molecules (fuels), pore space (the subsurface) and water, tracks projects on a seven step ladder from announcement to operation, and says what each story means for investors, regulators, industry and founders. Facts are sourced and dated; stages and outlooks are labeled as our judgment. General information, not investment advice.

## Tools
- [Energy and carbon footprint calculator](https://carbonenergynexus.com/calculator.html): households and companies, EPA and EIA factors, transparent Nexus Score
- [Frameworks](https://carbonenergynexus.com/frameworks.html): how projects, policy and carbon claims are judged

## Today's edition
- [COP31's draft deal asks the world to build 500 million tonnes of carbon capture by 2035](https://carbonenergynexus.com/): November 19, 2026. COP31's first draft deal asks countries to scale carbon capture to at least 500 million tonnes a year by 2035. The world runs about 68 million today. The EU and a bloc including Saudi Arabia and India want changes before talks close Nov 20.
- [Capital: North Carolina makes big data centers sign long contracts and pay for their own grid](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#money)
- [Projects: India gets a $3.6 billion green ammonia plant with buyers in hand](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#world)
- [Regulation: Colorado becomes the seventh state to permit its own CO2 storage wells](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#storage)
- [Water: AI's biggest water draw sits at the power plant, not the server hall](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#water)
- [Projects: Europe's first full cross-border CO2 chain is running, but the storage pipeline is thin](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#europe)
